item.title: Marvel's Wolverine is out — and the verdict is 'good, not great,' which is its own kind of story
item.description: Wolverine launched to a 78 Metacritic: brutal combat, but linear and short of Insomniac's Spider-Man highs. The honest day-one picture, now players have it.

item.title: Marvel's Wolverine is out tomorrow, the reviews are in, and Insomniac stuck the landing
item.description: Wolverine launches 15 September, hits 60fps with ray tracing on base PS5, and reviews praise its brutal combat. What is confirmed at launch.

item.title: The AI companies buying the chips are now saying slow down — and the chip stocks noticed
item.description: Anthropic and OpenAI are publicly calling to "pace the frontier." Semiconductor stocks are down 14% from June. What's happening, and why it matters.

item.title: Every official GTA 6 announcement, in order
item.description: A dated record of everything Rockstar and Take-Two have published about GTA 6, and deliberately nothing else.

item.title: Nintendo's Direct: a new Metroid, an open-world Kirby, and a Switch 2 calendar that fills up fast
item.description: Metroid Ravenous, Kirby and the World Beyond, Mega Man Dual Override, and a wall of Switch 2 dates. What Nintendo confirmed, and what it means.

item.title: The three big AI labs just shipped cyber-weapons — and locked the doors behind them
item.description: Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic each shipped a frontier cybersecurity model within weeks — and gated the most powerful features. What it means.

item.title: The GTA 6 PC question, answered honestly
item.description: No PC version is announced. What that means, what Rockstar's history suggests, and why every PC date circulating is invented.

item.title: Why your next PC, phone, and console just got more expensive — the memory crisis, explained
item.description: RAM prices are up over 100% and SSDs are climbing fast. It's not a shortage of chips — it's AI data centers eating the world's memory supply. What's confirmed.

item.title: Sony's GTA 6 controllers go up for pre-order today — here's what you actually get for $85
item.description: Two Vice City DualSense controllers, black and white, $84.99 each, out 19 November. Pre-orders open today. What's confirmed, and whether they're worth it.

item.title: Apple's foldable is real, it's called iPhone Duo, and it costs $1,999
item.description: Ternus's first keynote as CEO delivered the first foldable iPhone, the 18 Pro, and a split launch. Every confirmed price and date.

item.title: The other half of Apple's event: AirPods 5, Watch Series 12, and a big health push
item.description: Lost behind the foldable: AirPods 5 at $129 with real ANC, a re-architected Apple Watch, and an Apple Intelligence health system. The confirmed details.

item.title: Apple's event is tomorrow: how to watch, and the three things that actually matter
item.description: The "Surprise and Shine" keynote is 9 September, 10am Pacific. Start times worldwide, where to watch, and what to watch for beyond the phones.

item.title: GPT-6 Astra is here, and OpenAI spent most of the announcement warning about it
item.description: OpenAI's new flagship claims near-perfect reasoning scores and its first "Critical" cyber rating. It also costs 2.5x the last model. What's confirmed.

item.title: While GPT-6 got the headlines, Microsoft quietly made transcription almost free
item.description: MAI-Transcribe-2 costs $0.10 an audio hour — 72% less than five months ago. The unglamorous half of the AI market is where prices are actually falling.

item.title: The GTA 6 map: Rockstar finally gave a number, and it still isn't one
item.description: Three times Red Dead Redemption 2 is the first official word on the map. The problem is that RDR2's size was never official either.

item.title: Marvel's Wolverine is ten days out, and it's not the game people are expecting
item.description: Insomniac's Wolverine lands 15 September, PS5 exclusive. What's confirmed, and why it's darker than the Spider-Man comparison suggests.

item.title: Onimusha is back after twenty years — what the new one actually is
item.description: Onimusha: Way of the Sword is out, the first mainline entry in two decades. Here's what Capcom has revived, and who it's for.

item.title: The Blood of Dawnwalker: the vampire RPG that quietly opened this brutal month
item.description: The dark-fantasy RPG where you're part human, part vampire, and the clock is always running. What it is, and why it's worth attention in a crowded September.

item.title: Nvidia is buying Hugging Face, and it changes who controls open-source AI
item.description: A ~$12.9B definitive agreement puts the biggest open-model hub under the biggest AI chipmaker. What's confirmed, and why it's a bigger deal than the price.

item.title: State of Play: everything Sony actually announced, with the dates that are now locked
item.description: Two back-to-back showcases, a pile of release dates, and one long-awaited finale confirmed. What's confirmed from PlayStation's September State of Play.
